blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Logistics has many ways to go wrong. A truck breaks down. A ship is delayed. A driver is sick. A warehouse has a power cut. A border closes. A supplier fails at the worst time.

Risk management is simple. You need to know which problems are likely. You decide which ones matter most. Then you make a small plan for the serious ones. A contingency plan is a short document. It says: if X happens, we will do Y.

Nobody can stop all problems. But a team with a small, rehearsed plan reacts in minutes. A team without a plan reacts in hours.

items.q: What is a contingency plan?
options: A short document that says: if X happens, we will do Y
A list of all the company's trucks
A map of every border in the world
items.why: "A contingency plan is a short document. It says: if X happens, we will do Y."

items.q: According to the text, can risk management stop all problems?
options: No, nobody can stop all problems
No, because plans are too long
items.why: "Nobody can stop all problems." O plano ajuda a reagir, não a evitar tudo.

items.q: How fast does a team WITH a rehearsed plan react?
items.why: "a team with a small, rehearsed plan reacts in minutes".

items.q: The text suggests that having a plan is…
items.why: Inferência: o time com plano reage em minutos e o sem plano em horas — logo, ter plano é melhor.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which idea?
options: If you have a good plan, no problem will ever happen
Some risks matter more than others
A short plan can help a team react fast
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que ninguém pode parar todos os problemas — o plano só melhora a reação.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte explicando os planos ao novo líder de equipe. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hi, welcome to the team. Let me show you the three most common crises in our work, and the one-page plan for each.

Crisis one: a truck breaks down on the road. If a truck breaks down, we will call the backup driver and send a second truck. The plan is on the wall. It is short, so everyone can read it fast.

Crisis two: a ship is late at the port. If the ship is delayed, we will tell the client the same day and change the delivery date. We never wait. A late ship is normal, but a late message is a big problem.

Crisis three: a team member is sick. If someone is sick, we will move the work to two other people. Nobody works alone here.

Please read these three plans today. They are simple on purpose. A short plan that people remember is better than a long plan that nobody reads. And we will practise them next week, so we are ready.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How many common crises does Charlotte show the new team lead?
items.why: "the three most common crises… and the one-page plan for each."

items.q: What is the plan if a truck breaks down?
options: Ask the client to collect the goods
Wait for the truck to start again
Call the backup driver and send a second truck
items.why: "If a truck breaks down, we will call the backup driver and send a second truck."

items.q: What does Charlotte do when a ship is delayed?
options: She tells the client the same day and changes the date
She says nothing to the client
items.why: "If the ship is delayed, we will tell the client the same day and change the delivery date."

items.q: Why does Charlotte say the plans are 'simple on purpose'?
options: Because there is not enough paper
Because the boss does not like reading
Because a short plan is easier to remember and use
Because the team has no time to write long plans
items.why: Inferência: ela diz que um plano curto que as pessoas lembram é melhor que um longo que ninguém lê.

items.q: What can we understand about how this team works?
options: The team never practises the plans
People help each other and share the work
items.why: Inferência: "Nobody works alone here" e o trabalho é movido para outras pessoas — a equipe se apoia.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The old truck can break down in the cold." To break down means to…
items.why: To break down = quebrar, parar de funcionar.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "There was a ___, so the lights and computers went off."
items.why: Power cut = queda de energia; por isso luzes e computadores desligaram.

items.q: "A big storm can be a serious risk for our ships." A risk is…
options: a chance that something bad can happen
items.why: Risk = risco: a chance de algo ruim acontecer.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The ship is late, so there is a two-day ___."
items.why: Delay = atraso; o navio está atrasado dois dias.

items.q: "The team is rehearsed, so they act fast." Rehearsed means…
items.why: Rehearsed = ensaiado, que já treinou antes.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre riscos e planos. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The manager has to sign off on the new plan." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar oficialmente, dar o ok final.

items.q: "We will roll out the plan in every warehouse." To roll out means to…
options: start using it, step by step
items.why: Roll out = colocar em prática, aos poucos, em vários lugares.

items.q: "When the ship was late, the team had to deal with the problem fast." To deal with means to…
items.why: Deal with = lidar com, cuidar do problema.

items.q: "Please back up the driver if he is sick." To back up someone means to…
items.why: Back up = dar apoio, substituir ou ajudar alguém.

items.q: "We agreed the plan, but we did not follow through." This means we…
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.
